abstract: Spatial omics enables the integration of high-dimensional molecular organization with clinical outcomes, yet incorporating spatial single-cell information into predictive models at the population scale remains challenging. We introduce SPIN (spatial predictive integration network), which integrates subject-specific, cell-type level, spatially informed co-expression or co-abundance networks for population-scale clinical prediction. Current implementation of SPIN includes three key modules: network construction, molecular-to-clinical prediction by Bayesian scalar-on-network regression with manifold learning (BSNMani), and visualization & interpretation module. In the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) transcriptomics cohort, SPIN achieved an accuracy of 0.81 for dementia-status prediction and revealed co-expression subnetworks with clear biological relevance. SPIN also achieved robust survival prediction in a breast cancer single-cell proteomics cohort (C-index = 0.78), identifying two survival-associated spatial proteomic subnetworks. In summary, SPIN is an interpretable tool for spatial-omics-based clinical outcome prediction at the population scale.
